name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
description: NIST CSF 2.0 baseline overlay — always active for all agents. The AKSIs are organized by CSF functions, making this the most direct and natural mapping. Provides CSF-specific evidence packaging for organizations demonstrating framework alignment.

evidence_requirements: Organizational cybersecurity policy established and communicated (GV.PO-01)
Policy reviewed and updated at defined intervals (GV.PO-02)
Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities established and communicated (GV.RR-01)
Cybersecurity roles coordinated and aligned across the organization (GV.RR-02)
Risk management strategy established describing risk tolerance (GV.RM-01)
Risk appetite and tolerance statements communicated (GV.RM-02)
Oversight of cybersecurity risk management exercised by appropriate parties (GV.OV-01)
Cybersecurity risk management activities reviewed (GV.OV-02)
Hardware and software assets inventoried (ID.AM-01)
Assets prioritized based on classification and criticality (ID.AM-02)
Platforms and software applications inventoried (ID.AM-02)
External information systems catalogued (ID.AM-05)
Data at rest and in transit identified and classified (ID.AM-07)
Data lifecycle management practices established (ID.AM-08)
Supply chain risk management strategy established (ID.SC-01)
Suppliers and third parties assessed for cybersecurity risk (ID.SC-02)
Vulnerabilities in assets identified and documented (ID.RA-01)
Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts used to determine risk (ID.RA-02)
Identities and credentials for authorized users and services managed (PR.AA-01)
Access permissions and authorizations managed with least privilege (PR.AA-03)
Access permissions enforced with least privilege and separation of duties (PR.AA-01)
Access to assets managed, monitored, and enforced (PR.AA-05)
Data-at-rest and data-in-transit protected (PR.DS-01)
Assets formally managed throughout lifecycle (PR.DS-02)
Data-at-rest and data-in-transit protected (PR.DS-01)
Data integrity checking mechanisms applied (PR.DS-02)
Audit/log records determined, documented, implemented, and reviewed (DE.AE-02)
Information from multiple sources aggregated and analyzed (DE.AE-06)
Configuration baselines established and maintained (PR.PS-01)
Software installed and configurations managed per security standards (PR.PS-02)
Data-at-rest protected including encryption (PR.DS-01)
Data-in-transit protected including encryption (PR.DS-02)
Data-at-rest and data-in-transit protected from unauthorized modification (PR.DS-01)
Input validation and sanitization practices applied (PR.DS-02)
Anomalous activity detected in a timely manner (DE.AE-02)
Events from multiple sources correlated for analysis (DE.AE-06)
Network and environment monitored for cybersecurity events (DE.CM-01)
Computing hardware and software monitored for configuration changes (DE.CM-09)
Anomalous activity detected and analyzed for event characterization (DE.AE-02)
Information from multiple sources aggregated for posture assessment (DE.AE-06)
Computing platforms monitored for integrity (DE.CM-09)
Event data integrity verified
Incident response plan executed during or after an incident (RS.MA-01)
Incident reports provided to designated stakeholders (RS.MA-02)
Response activities coordinated with internal and external stakeholders (RS.CO-02)
Information shared with designated authorities as required (RS.CO-03)
Investigation of incidents conducted to support response (RS.AN-03)
Incidents are categorized consistent with response plans (RS.AN-06)
Recovery plan executed during or after an incident (RC.RP-01)
Recovery actions confirmed and communicated (RC.RP-02)
Recovery planning and processes improved incorporating lessons learned (RC.IM-01)
Recovery strategies updated based on experience (RC.IM-02)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: NIST CSF is voluntary. No formal certification or assessment requirement. Organizations self-assess alignment using CSF Profiles (Current and Target). Third-party assessments optional. The Framework is used to communicate risk posture, not for pass/fail compliance.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: No mandatory reporting entity. CSF Profiles used internally and shared with stakeholders as needed.

human_oversight_mandates.description: NIST CSF 2.0 does not mandate specific human oversight configurations. Individual subcategories (GV.OV, RS.CO) reference oversight and communication but do not prescribe specific human-in-the-loop requirements.

notes: NIST CSF 2.0 is the most widely adopted cybersecurity framework globally. The AKSIs are explicitly organized by CSF 2.0 functions (GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER), making this the cleanest and most natural mapping. NIST CSF evidence is about demonstrating alignment, not pass/fail compliance. This overlay is always active as a baseline — it does not set strict thresholds or additional evidence requirements beyond what baseline controls already provide.
